whitewash: A white liquid that people put on walls to make them white.
lowly: Small and not grand or important.
divine: Very special, as if it came from God.
imperiously: In a proud way that expects people to do what is said.
carriage: An old kind of vehicle that horses pull, with seats for people.
scrabble: Moved the hands or feet fast against something, to get through.
caress: Touched very softly and with love.
cellarage: Rooms under a house, below the ground, where things are kept.
chaff: Joking with someone in a friendly way and laughing at them.
sinuous: Having many smooth bends, one after the other.
scull: One of the light oars used to move a small boat.
sculled: Moved a small boat by pulling light oars through the water.
painter: A rope at the front of a boat, used to fasten it to the bank.
gingerly: With great care, afraid that you might fall or be hurt.
rowlock: A part on the side of a boat that holds an oar in place.
wicker: Thin sticks put together to make things such as chairs.
moorhen: A small dark bird that lives by the water.
weasel: A very small, thin animal with a long body that kills other small animals for food.
stoat: A small, thin animal with brown fur, like a weasel; it kills other small animals.
punt: To move a flat boat along by pushing a long stick against the bottom of the river.
stability: The quality of not changing or moving easily.
errant: Going from place to place, or going the wrong way.
bedraggled: Wet and messy, with clothes or hair out of place.
ass: An animal like a small horse with long ears. Here it means a silly person.
implore: Asked in a very strong way, because of great need.
drake: The male bird of a kind that swims on water and says 'quack'.
slushy: Soft, wet and sticky, like earth after rain.
undergrowth: Small plants and low branches growing thickly under tall trees.
larder: A cool room or place where food is kept.
nudge: Touched someone softly with the arm, to tell them something.
gipsy: A person who travels from place to place and lives in a small house that a horse pulls.
caravan: A small house that a horse pulls along the road.
heath: Wild, open land with low plants and no trees.
bunk: A narrow bed fixed to a wall, as on a boat.
locker: A small box or space with a door, for keeping things.
baccy: A dried plant that people smoke. A friendly, everyday word.
imploringly: In a way that asks very strongly for help.
fusty: Old and closed in, with a bad scent, as a room is when the windows are never opened.
doggedly: Not giving up, in a firm way.
nosebag: A bag with food in it, put on a horse's head so that it can eat.
platter: A big flat thing for putting food on at the table.
drone: A low sound that goes on and on, without stopping.
brazen: Loud and rough, like the sound of metal.
highwayman: A man on a horse who stopped people on the road and took their money.
mariner: A man who works on a ship at sea.
axle: The long bar under a cart that the round parts at each end turn on.
miry: Wet and soft, full of sticky earth.
diffident: Not sure of yourself and afraid to speak out.
debonair: Happy, nice and easy in the way you act.
jerkin: A short coat without arms, worn long ago.
languorous: Slow and tired, because it is hot.
masquerade: A party where people cover their faces and wear special clothes.
quickset: Small trees or plants set close together in a line and growing thick.
billowy: Rising and falling in big soft rolls, like the sea.
drapery: Cloth that falls down in soft, long pieces.
golosh: A cover worn over your boots in wet weather to keep out water.
pitfall: A hole in the ground that you cannot see and that can hurt you.
faery: Like a place in a fairy story, full of magic. Here it is used for the snow.
bole: The thick main part of a tree, standing up from the ground.
rodent: A small animal with sharp front teeth that it uses to bite things.
bellpull: A handle or rope at a door that you pull to tell people inside that you are there.
shuffle: To walk slowly, pulling the feet along the floor.
hearth: The floor in front of a fire in a room.
settle: A long seat made of wood, with a high back.
trestle: A frame made of wood, with legs, that holds up the top of a table.
dresser: A tall thing made of wood, with places one above another for keeping cups and things for the table.
rafter: A long piece of wood that holds up the top of a house.
repast: Food that you sit down to eat.
embers: Small pieces of wood that are still red and hot after a fire is nearly out.
arduous: Very hard and making you very tired.
loft: A room just under the top of a house.
rasher: A thin piece of a special kind of meat that people cook for breakfast.
somnolence: The feeling of being ready to sleep.
obliterate: Made something go away completely, so that nothing can be seen.
bramble: A wild plant with sharp points on it that hurt your skin.
stile: Steps that let people go over a wall, but not animals.
furrow: A long line cut in the earth by a farmer's tool, for the seeds.
hurdle: Sticks joined together to make a light wall in a field.
casement: A window that opens like a door.
latticed: Made of crossed thin pieces of wood or metal with spaces between.
smouldering: Giving off smoke and heat, but without a bright fire.
appurtenance: A small thing that goes with a bigger thing.
plumage: All the soft covering of a bird's body.
sleet: Cold rain with small bits of ice in it.
filament: A very thin line, as thin as a hair.
waft: A light movement of air that carries a scent or a sound.
submissively: In a way that does what you are told, without arguing.
beguile: To make time pass in a nice way, or to win someone with charm.
sanded: Covered on the floor with tiny dry pieces of stone, like those on a beach.
skittle: A game in which you roll a ball to hit tall pieces of wood standing in a row.
cockleshell: The shell of a small sea animal, used here as a shape for a pattern.
fallow: Left with nothing growing for a time, as a field is.
benison: A good wish for someone, asking for God's kindness.
bashful: Afraid to speak to people, and easily made to feel awkward.
peal: A long, loud ringing sound, such as from a church tower.
chilblain: A red place on the skin of the hands or feet that hurts, caused by cold.
mull: To warm a drink and add sugar and other things to it.
corsair: A man who attacks ships at sea to take what is on them.
galley: An old ship that men moved by pulling long oars.
coax: Tried to get someone to do something by being gentle and kind.
swathe: A long line of cut grass or grain.
wonted: As always; the same as every other time.
varnish: Putting a clear, shiny liquid on wood to make it look good.
solemnity: A serious and very quiet way of acting.
trustworthy: That you can believe and count on.
gaiters: Covers worn on the lower legs, from the foot up, to keep them clean and dry.
gauntleted: Wearing long, thick covers on the hands.
outrage: A very bad act that makes people very angry.
blustering: Talking in a loud way and saying how great you are, but without real strength.
panoply: A full set of clothes or equipment, grand to look at.
furrowed: Marked with deep lines, like the earth cut by a farmer's tool.
gratified: Pleased, because you got what you wanted.
scandalised: Very surprised and angry, because something seems very wrong.
uncouth: Rough and strange, and not polite.
mullion: A bar that goes up and down in the middle of a window and holds the glass in parts.
caustic: Sharp and unkind in the way it finds fault.
crestfallen: Sad and shamed because you did not get what you hoped.
turbid: Not clear, because of earth stirred up in it, as water can be.
ancestral: Passed down in a family from people who lived long ago.
rogue: A bad man who tells lies and takes what is not his.
ruffian: A rough man who may hurt people.
dock: The place in a court where the person who is said to have done wrong stands.
lenient: Not hard on people who have done wrong; kind in what you decide.
